title: An invitation for the weekend
prompt: Write an email inviting a friend to spend Saturday afternoon with you. Suggest an activity, explain where to meet, and ask whether the time is convenient.
checklist: Greet your friend.
Explain the activity, place and time.
Ask a question and end politely.

title: Your favorite corner
prompt: Describe a place at home where you feel comfortable. Include what it looks like, what you do there, and why you enjoy it.
checklist: Introduce the place.
Include two concrete details.
Explain how the place makes you feel.

title: A recipe for a friend
prompt: A friend wants to try a simple dish from your home. Write an email explaining the ingredients and the main cooking steps. Include one useful tip.
checklist: Name the dish and main ingredients.
Put the steps in a clear order.
Add a practical tip and a friendly ending.

title: The unexpected bus stop
prompt: Write a short story beginning with: I got off the bus and realized I was in the wrong place. Describe what happened and how the situation ended.
checklist: Set the scene using the opening sentence.
Describe a problem and an action.
Give the story a clear ending.

title: A better team routine
prompt: Write to your team leader suggesting one change to your weekly meetings. Explain the current problem, your proposal, and one likely benefit.
checklist: Use a polite opening.
Explain the problem and proposal.
End with a clear request for feedback.

title: Small habits, better days
prompt: Some people think improving daily wellbeing requires a major lifestyle change. Write a paragraph giving your view and two examples of manageable habits.
checklist: State your opinion clearly.
Support it with two everyday examples.
Connect the examples to a concluding idea.

title: A tool worth keeping
prompt: Describe a digital tool you find useful. Explain how you use it, who else might benefit, and one limitation people should know about.
checklist: Introduce the tool and its purpose.
Describe a realistic use case.
Mention a limitation without losing focus.

title: A neighborhood with less waste
prompt: Should local communities focus more on reusing items than on recycling them? Explain your position, consider a counterargument, and suggest a practical action.
checklist: Present a clear position.
Develop a reason and address a counterargument.
Conclude with a realistic local action.

title: Learning by doing
prompt: Compare structured courses and independent projects as ways to learn a new skill. Argue for an approach or combination, using specific examples.
checklist: Define the two approaches.
Compare their strengths with examples.
Give a balanced recommendation.

title: The message in the old notebook
prompt: Write a story about someone who finds a note they wrote years earlier. Show how their understanding of success has changed through an encounter or decision.
checklist: Introduce the notebook and its owner.
Develop a meaningful encounter or decision.
Show the change through actions or details.
